answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared harbor fund before it earns rewards, with the stake growing along a ridge of proven work: every completed job adds verifiable history, like trees planted in an orchard that only bear fruit after seasons of care. An attacker spinning up thousands of fresh identities pays the full stake for each one and earns nothing until each builds its own history, so flooding the network costs far more than any reward it could harvest, while honest agents keep their stake and compound trust.
